content:
We have already studied Korah, and then Dathan and Abiram, and how they rebelled against Moses and Aaron. But their rebellion did not remain the rebellion of only a few men. As they lifted up their voices against Yahweh's appointed servants, they drew the people with them. Numbers 16:19 tells us that Korah "gathered all the congregation against them at the door of the tabernacle of meeting." This is a solemn thing to notice. It was not only Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, and the two hundred and fifty leaders who stood against Moses. Korah was able to gather the whole congregation. The complaint of a few had spread until a whole nation was leaning toward rebellion. This is how a hard heart begins to spread. One voice complains, and others listen.

The complaint sounds reasonable, and soon many are gathered around it.The people had heard Korah's words so often that they began to believe them, and they came out and stood against the very men God had appointed to lead them.

Then the glory of Yahweh appeared to all the congregation. Yahweh was ready to consume them, but Moses and Aaron fell on their faces and pleaded, "O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and You be angry with all the congregation?" (Numbers 16:22). Even as the people gathered against him, Moses was still praying for them. Yahweh then told the congregation to move away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Moses warned the people not even to touch anything that belonged to these men. And then Moses said something that placed the whole matter into Yahweh's hands. He said that if these men died a natural death, then Yahweh had not sent him. But if Yahweh did something entirely new, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, then everyone would know that these men had despised Yahweh (Numbers 16:28-30). The moment Moses finished speaking, the ground split apart. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed Korah's household, Dathan, Abiram, and all who belonged to the rebellion, and they went down alive into the pit (Numbers 16:31-33). Then fire came out from Yahweh and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who had presumptuously offered incense (Numbers 16:35). The judgment was sudden, visible, and undeniable.

All Israel who were around them fled at their cry, for they said, "Lest the earth swallow us up also!" (Numbers 16:34).

Now consider carefully what the people had just seen with their own eyes.

They had seen the ground tear open. They had seen men swallowed alive.They had heard the terrible cry. They had seen fire fall from Yahweh and consume two hundred and fifty leaders in an instant. Surely, after witnessing such a fearful judgment, the people would never dare to rebel again.Surely their hearts would melt in the fear of Yahweh. But this is exactly where the passage becomes deeply sobering. Numbers 16:41 says, "On the next day all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, You have killed the people of Yahweh." It was not many days later.It was the very next morning. The ground where their neighbours had been swallowed was still fresh. The memory of the fire was less than a day old.And yet the people rose up again, and this time they blamed Moses and Aaron for the deaths, calling the rebels "the people of Yahweh." They looked at men whom Yahweh Himself had judged, and called them Yahweh's people.They looked at Yahweh's own act of judgment, and blamed His servants for it. This is what a hardened heart does. It sees the clearest evidence and still refuses to bend.

How could this happen? How could a people see such a thing and remain unchanged? The answer is that a hard heart is not softened merely by seeing. Pharaoh saw ten plagues and hardened himself again and again.

These Israelites saw the earth open, and hardened themselves within a single day. This teaches us a fearful truth: witnessing the judgment of God does not automatically soften the heart. If the heart is already set against Yahweh, even the most terrible sight can be explained away, resented, or turned into a fresh accusation. The people did not fall down in repentance. They did not cry,"We have sinned." Instead, they found someone to blame. And notice how quickly a hardened heart forgets. Only hours before, the whole camp had fled in terror, crying that the earth might swallow them too. Yet by the next morning that terror had already turned into anger, and the anger was aimed not at their own sin, but at Moses and Aaron. The Scripture warns us plainly, "Today, if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts" (Hebrews 3:15). And again it says, "He who is often rebuked, and hardens his neck, will suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy" (Proverbs 29:1). Israel had been rebuked in the most fearful way possible, yet they hardened their necks, and the plague that followed took the lives of fourteen thousand seven hundred people (Numbers 16:49).

So, we see the terrible progress of a hardened heart. It begins by listening to a complaint. Then it joins the complaint. Then it stands with the rebellion.

Then, even when Yahweh's judgment falls in plain sight, it refuses to repent and instead searches for someone to blame. The people had every reason to fear Yahweh and turn back to Him, yet their hearts had become like stone. They had heard rebellion so long that Yahweh's own voice no longer moved them.This is the great danger of a heart that is fed on murmuring and complaint. Little by little it grows hard, until even the fire of Yahweh and the opening of the earth cannot break it. This is a searching lesson, and it does not belong only to Israel. The same hardness can grow quietly in us. We too can see the judgments of God in the world around us and remain unmoved. We too can witness His dealings and still find someone else to blame. Tomorrow, Yahweh willing, we will study our own hearts, and see how we, the New Creation, can become stone-hearted like Israel, even after seeing the hand of God at work.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, whose judgments are true and whose mercy is great,
We tremble to see a people witness Your power and harden their hearts by the very next morning.

Guard us from listening so long to complaint that Your own voice no longer moves us.

Keep us from blaming others for the fruit of our own sin, as Israel blamed Moses and Aaron.

Soften our hearts today, while it is still called today, that we may hear Your voice.

Let us not harden our necks under Your rebuke, but fall down and truly repent.

"Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts." - Hebrews 3:15

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
